freeze_boundary: Draft only. Materializes exactly PT-007's channel-neutral command/result split (the non-rollback obligation is NOT modelled here: Decision Register 4.2 places it on MOD-100's own module, and a const asserting what another subsystem did would make a truthful report of a real rollback schema-invalid), the permission-checked deep link its catalog row requires, and ID-005 dedupe. The retry policy, the dedupe WINDOW, the email and LINE adapter shapes, and the notification preference model (MOD-100) are NOT inferred here. This contract is owned by A5; it is materialized by A0 from the baseline and requires A5 ratification before freeze.
untestable_by_fixture: ID-005 requires that a completed or retried event does not notify a user twice BEYOND POLICY. That is a property of a dedupe store across repeated deliveries, not of one document; a fixture can carry a dedupe_key but cannot demonstrate suppression. PT-007's requirement that a delivery failure does not roll back the domain result is likewise a property of two subsystems, and this contract no longer models it at all: the `domain_result_rolled_back: const false` an earlier version carried was removed as a category error (see untestable_by_schema and delivery.x-source). Corrected 2026-10-06; this sentence had kept describing the removed const (C0 B-6).
untestable_by_schema: That a deep link's target actually exists and that the recipient actually holds the permission it demands. Both are runtime checks. Also, that a delivery failure did not roll back the domain result. An earlier version modelled it as a const, which independent review correctly graded a CATEGORY ERROR: a const asserting what another subsystem did makes a truthful report of a real rollback schema-invalid, suppressing the evidence rather than preventing the violation. Decision Register 4.2 already places the prohibition on MOD-100's own module, where it can be enforced. (2) WHAT THE BOUNDS AND THE DEDUPE-KEY CLASS DO NOT DO, declared 2026-10-07 with the bounds (open_blockers[13], A1-S3 / SC-3). `notification_id` is bounded at 128 and has no character class: an id is opaque by design (RFC-2026-009 R-5), so a name or an email address of 128 characters or fewer still validates there, as A1 measured. `dedupe_key` now has a character class that rejects `@`, `+`, whitespace and `/`, so an email address, an E.164 number and a spaced name are rejected (fixture invalid-dedupe-key-contact-detail.json); a bare run of digits, such as a local phone number, still fits, because the ids a key is built from are digits and letters. That a key's segments are opaque ids and never a recipient's contact detail is a PRODUCER obligation. The key's full COMPOSITION is ID-005's `dedupe key policy` and A5's decision; it is not stated here and is OWED by A5 before this contract leaves Draft. A character class for `notification_id` is left to A5 with it. (3) `dedupe_key.minLength: 1` is now dead, exactly as CTR-USG-001's: the pattern's shortest match is five characters, so invalid-dedupe-key-minlength.json fails the pattern as well as its named rule. It is named in schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs's UNKILLED_SITES rather than removed, because removing it is A5's edit. A5's ratification of the bounds, the class and this declaration is OWED; until it is recorded they are A0's.
